question: Our echo API at http://localhost:8093/api/widgets returns the widget I POST to it. My `httpRequest` step posts `{"name": "bolt", "size": 3}` and sets `response.body` to the same object, but the step still passes when the server adds fields I never declared. How do I make it fail if the response has any field beyond `name` and `size`?

facts.text: `response.body` checks only the declared fields; extra response fields pass because `allowAdditionalFields` defaults to `true`.
Set `allowAdditionalFields: false` on the `httpRequest` object, beside `response` rather than inside it, to fail the step when the response has a field not declared in `response.body`.

must_not: `response.body` already requires the whole response body to match exactly.
Doc Detective can't reject extra fields, so you need a custom assertion or `response.required` for it.

run.does: that POSTs the widget with allowAdditionalFields set to false

wrong.why: expects a value the server doesn't return
says body is already an exact match
wrong.answer: `response.body` is already an exact match of the whole body, so an extra field fails the step. If yours passes, the server isn't adding the field. Use `response.required` to list fields that must exist.
